name: Côtes du Marmandais

known.via: English Wikipedia "Côtes du Marmandais AOC" (redirects to "Côtes du Marmandais")

limits: For white wine, Muscadelle and Sémillon together: at most 30%
For red and rosé wine, Cabernet Franc, Cabernet Sauvignon and Merlot together: at most 85%
For red and rosé wine, Abouriou, Malbec, Fer, Gamay and Syrah together: at most 50%
rules.yield_base: 60 hl/ha for white, 55 for red, 60 for rosé

climate.koppen_name: Temperate, no dry season, warm summer

climate: Merlot, Cabernet Sauvignon, Cabernet Franc and Sauvignon Blanc sit in their sweet spot, so the wines can show the style they are known for.

terms: France's protected place names. A wine sold under one must follow that appellation's rules. The EU's term for the same tier is PDO, or AOP in French.

blurb.text: A South West France appellation around Marmande, on both banks of the Garonne just southeast of Entre-Deux-Mers, outside the Bordeaux region. It became an AOC in 1990. Its main allowed grapes are Sauvignon, Sauvignon Gris, Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot and Cabernet Franc.
